blocks.text: Humans are endothermic homeotherms. They regulate body temperature through negative feedback mechanism. For example; the thermoreceptors present in skin detect an increase or decrease in body temperature. They send signals to the control centre i.e., hypothalamus which also contains thermoreceptors. Hypothalamus sends signals to muscles and glands which produce corrective responses e.g.,

When body temperature rises above 37°C (hyperthermia), vasodilation occurs. It is the expansion of blood capillaries which lie just beneath the epidermis of the skin. So, there is more flow of blood in these capillaries to remove more heat from blood. Responses also include sweating. Evaporation of sweat carries heat from the body and produces cooling effect. The thyroid gland may decrease the secretion of thyroxine, which lowers the basal metabolic rate. So, the internal heat production is reduced.
book_errors: It is the expansion of blood capillaries

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Capillaries have no muscle in their walls and cannot widen themselves. In vasodilation the arterioles (small arteries) that supply the skin capillaries widen, so more blood flows through the capillaries just beneath the epidermis and more heat is lost from the skin.
The thermoreceptors also stimulate the higher centres of brain. So, we 'feel' warmth or coldness. It allows us to take more actions like taking a bath or turning the fans or heaters on.

When body temperature falls below 37°C (hypothermia), the responses may include vasoconstriction, shivering and increase in metabolic rate. Vasoconstriction reduces blood flow to the skin and so there is less loss of heat from blood. Shivering (spasmodic contraction of skeletal muscles) produces heat which helps to raise the body temperature. Tiny muscles at the base of hair follicles contract (goosebumps). Air is trapped in the erected hair and act as insulator for the heat. Increased metabolic rate also produces heat to raise the body temperature.

blocks.alt: Two loops around a see-saw 'Body Temp. 37 C (homeostasis)'. Upper loop: body temperature increases above normal; receptors in skin and hypothalamus detect it; the control centre in the hypothalamus acts on effectors, sweat production and vasodilation; temperature decreases to normal. Lower loop: temperature decreases below normal; receptors detect it; the control centre acts on vasoconstriction and shivering; temperature increases to normal.
blocks.caption: Figure 13.5: Thermoregulation in humans (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 13.5).
blocks.long_description: Each loop runs from a stimulus box through 'Receptors (in skin & hypothalamus) detect stimulus' and 'Information sent to control centre.' to a brain with the hypothalamus marked, then to the effectors and a response box. Hot loop effectors: a skin section with a coiled sweat gland and a drop on the surface, 'Sweat production: Cooling by evaporation.', and a skin section with widened vessels near the surface and heat arrows, 'Vasodilation: Heat radiated from skin surface.'. Cold loop effectors: a skin section with narrow, deeper vessels, 'Vasoconstriction: Blood diverted to deep tissues to minimize heat loss.', and skeletal muscle fibres, 'Shivering in skeletal muscles: Heat produced.'. Both see-saw ends are marked 'Imbalance'.
